title: A day of rest
hook: your sabbath: when, how, what instead
tomorrow: an emperor came to see the Guru. why did he eat on the floor first?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: my day, on one page, small enough to keep. The daily practice is gathered. Now the week, starting with a day people love to argue about.

Ask a few friends what a day off is for and you'll get an argument. Recharge, so you work better. Do nothing, on principle. Finally catch up on errands. The Bible gives the Sabbath commandment twice, and the two tellings don't give the same reason. In Exodus it begins: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. In Deuteronomy, when Moses repeats the commandments to the people, it begins: Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it. Remember, and keep. Then each one explains why, and the explanations part ways.
screen: `WHAT IS A DAY OFF FOR?` → `TOLD TWICE.` → `REMEMBER.` → `KEEP.`

segments.voice: Exodus says: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day. Rest here is holy time. You stop because God stopped. The day is set apart, a piece of time that belongs to God. Deuteronomy says something else. Your servants rest too, and your ox and your donkey, that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou. And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt. Rest here is freedom. Slaves don't get a day off. Free people do, and they give it to everyone under their roof. So which is it? One side says the Sabbath is first about holiness: without the holy, it shrinks into a long weekend. The other side says it is first about justice: a weekly reminder that nobody is a machine, and the worker rests as well as the boss. The rabbis refused to choose. The Talmud teaches that remember and keep were spoken by God in one utterance, and on Friday nights the hymn Lecha Dodi still sings it. That is why Shabbat is kept both ways at once: as holy time, with candles and blessing, and as a day of no work for anyone in the house.
screen: `EXODUS: BECAUSE GOD RESTED.` · `DEUTERONOMY: YOU WERE SLAVES.` · `HOLINESS, OR JUSTICE?` · `ONE UTTERANCE: REMEMBER AND KEEP.` · then, large: `REST DAY.`

segments.voice: Choose your rest day, and the hour it begins. Name one kind of work you won't do on it, the one most likely to creep in anyway, and what you'll do instead when it does, something that makes the day feel set apart. Then let the plan settle while you breathe.
A day of rest: one day a week set apart from work, holy because God rested, and free because no one should be a slave.
Here's the line: rest day, remembered and kept, both at the same time. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews keep Shabbat from Friday sundown to Saturday night as holy time, with candles, blessings and prayer, and as a day without work for the whole household; the Friday-night hymn Lecha Dodi sings of 'remember' and 'keep' said as one.

fork.setup: your coworker says the Sabbath is only about worship and has nothing to do with workers. what's the best case for the other reading?
options: Deuteronomy grounds it in slavery: your servant rests as well as you.
Exodus says God rested because the work had worn him out.
the commandment only applied to priests working in the temple.
fork.reveal: Deuteronomy's reason is freedom: you were slaves in Egypt, so everyone in your house rests. The rabbis kept that reason next to Exodus' holiness, not instead of it.

what it means: the Sabbath has two reasons, holy time because God rested, and freedom because slaves get no day off.
what a scholar hears: Exodus 20:8-11 grounds it in creation, Deuteronomy 5:12-15 in the exodus from Egypt; the Talmud's 'one utterance' is in Shevuot 20b, sung in Lecha Dodi.

chat.says: new day off: monday. theo says use it to job hunt. inés says rest is a right. who's right?
options: keep it free of work, like Deuteronomy, and set apart, like Exodus.
Theo: rest is there so the other six days are more productive.
neither: a rest day only counts if you spend it at home alone.
chat.meaning: The Sabbath is given twice: Exodus makes it holy because God rested; Deuteronomy makes it free because slaves get no day off. The rabbis kept both.

tie.story: The Bible gives the Sabbath twice: remember it because God rested, keep it because you were slaves.
tie.friend: Zoe's Monday can be both: no job hunting, and one thing that makes it feel set apart.
tie.you: what would make your rest day feel set apart, not just empty?
